terms.gloss: a weapon; properly one that is thrown
evidence: Cic. Mil. 11: esse cum tēlō hominis occīdendī causā (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Properly a missile, a spear or a dart; then any weapon for striking, a sword or an axe (Lewis & Short). Weapons in general are arma.
Plural only: properly the arms for defence and close fighting, then weapons of every kind (Lewis & Short). To take up arms, arma capere; to hand in one’s weapons, arma trādere (Traupman 185, 188).

phrases.latin: Ēripere tēlum, nōn dare īrātō decet.
phrases.english: Take the weapon away from an angry man; don’t hand it to him.

phrases.latin: ūsus equī nunc est, levibus nunc lūditur armīs, nunc pila, nunc celerī volvitur orbe trochus
phrases.english: now is the time for riding, now for games with light weapons, now for the ball, now the hoop goes rolling round

sources: Lewis & Short: telum · Lewis & Short: arma
